card.title: The Debt Changes Hands
card.instruction: Treat every favor as shifting who owes whom. Recalculate the balance whenever help is accepted, refused, or remembered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You fixed my bike, so I owe you dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was repaying the dinner you cooked last week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then your repair was too good. I owe you for the surplus kindness.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you're saving me work. The debt has increased.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 bike repair creates debt, A3 past dinner offsets only part of its quality and A5 refusing dinner adds saved-labor debt.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 prior repayment leads A3 surplus kindness; B4 no-cooking request becomes A5 another favor.

relationship.evidence: B2 tries to settle reciprocal help and B4 refuses an unwanted repeat meal.

heightening.evidence: B4 attempt to stop the cycle increases A5 the very debt it was meant to end.

specificity.evidence: A1 bike repair and B2 earlier dinner establish the favor account concretely.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 saved work is an earned inversion of B4 refusal without explaining why the cooking is unwanted.
